To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the spatial alignment effect influences maximal finger aperture only when cup is located in near space; (2) cup distance influences temporal and kinematic parameters of the movement, regardless the actual possibility to reach it.

(1) the spatial alignment effect influences kinematic parameters of reach-to-grasp movements when the object is located near the hand but not when it is located far; (2) the effect depends on the influence exerted by the size of the object body, when it is located near the grasp hand; (3) cup distance (extrinsic property) influences affordance, independently from the possibility to actually execute the movement.

1) the spatial alignment effect is not limited to the actual execution of a reaching-grasping action but it is also effective when the action is pantomimed; 2) the effect is effective only when the action is executed in the near space, i.e. when the target is reachable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of object affordance on pantomime execution, and the role of object distance (extrinsic property) on the control of the movement.
the study of the spatial alignment effect and its influence on kinematics of reach-to-grasp movement.
the study of the relationship between action observation and action execution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, when executing the reach-to-grasp task, affordance is instantiated, but it is influenced by both the intrinsic properties of the object and the possibility of actually reaching it.
, when executing pantomimes, the affordance related to object use was activated only in the peripersonal and reachable space.

the spatial alignment effect is not only an affordance effect but it is an affordance related to a possible interaction between the agent and the environment, and that the affordance is influenced by the possibility of interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reach-to-grasp affordance is not only influenced by the object properties (i.e. the cup handle orientation and the cup distance), but also by the possibility to actually interact with the object.
the affordance related to an object is not only a property of that object (intrinsic) but it is also related to its spatial relationship with the observer (extrinsic).
, during the execution of pantomime, the affordance related to object’s use is instantiated, but the actual possibility to reach the target is necessary to make it effective.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the affordance of a target object is not a static property, but is dynamically influenced by the interaction of intrinsic properties (e.g. spatial alignment of object features and the body) and extrinsic properties (e.g., the object distance).
the spatial alignment effect is not only a motor control mechanism but also a mechanism that influences the perception-action system.
, during a reach-to-grasping pantomime, the spatial alignment effect can be modulated by the possibility to reach the target.
